questions.question_text: When crafting a short 1-2 minute presentation about yourself for a job interview at a local pet store, what is the BEST way to structure your talk to make a strong impression?
You’re interviewing for a summer camp counsellor position and want to use a visual to support your presentation. Which of the following is the MOST effective way to use a prop during your talk?

options.text: Bring a large scrapbook with every photo from your life and flip through it while speaking.
Show a single photo of you leading a group of kids at an event, briefly explain its relevance (“This scavenger hunt taught me patience”), and then refocus on your words.
Use a slideshow with 15 slides full of tiny text and read every word directly off the screen.
Hold up a random object, like a toy, without explaining why it matters to your story.

questions.question_text: Before giving a class presentation, you feel your heart racing and your hands shaking. Which technique from Chapter 9 is the MOST effective immediate way to calm your nerves right before you start speaking?

options.text: Tell yourself, “I’m going to mess up,” to prepare for the worst.
Use the “4-7-8” breathing method: Inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 7, exhale for 8, and repeat 3-5 times.
Avoid practicing beforehand so you don’t overthink it.
Focus on every person in the audience staring at you to stay alert.

questions.question_text: Imagine you’re preparing for a scholarship interview. How can you combine skills from all sections of Chapter 9 to make the strongest impact?

options.text: Memorize a long speech without practicing it aloud and bring 10 unrelated props to show off.
Prepare a structured 1-2 minute talk about your achievements, use one relevant visual like a certificate to highlight a key point, and practice deep breathing to manage nerves.
Focus only on visuals by creating a 20-slide presentation and skip talking about yourself.
Avoid preparing a personal story and just answer whatever questions come up without a plan.
